paragraphs: A diffusion model can describe plausible data, but using it to generate samples that also satisfy a separate constraint creates a difficult inference problem. The desired distribution combines the model’s prior with a black-box likelihood or constraint function. This paper studies how to train a sampler for that combined distribution, spreading the cost of inference across subsequent samples.

The proposed objective, relative trajectory balance, comes from viewing diffusion models through the framework of generative flow networks. It provides a data-free way to train a diffusion model toward the desired posterior. The authors prove asymptotic correctness: the guarantee concerns the limiting behavior of the method, rather than exact sampling after any finite amount of training. This perspective also enables reinforcement learning techniques intended to improve coverage of different modes.

Experiments cover classifier-guided images, language infilling, and text-to-image generation. The authors also apply the method to continuous control with a learned behavior prior, reporting state-of-the-art offline reinforcement learning results. Together, these findings support the approach’s potential across several forms of constrained generation and decision-making.
neurips-2024-amortizing-intractable-infe.tldr: Relative trajectory balance trains diffusion models to sample constrained posteriors with an asymptotic correctness guarantee and promising results across generation and control.

paragraphs: Text-to-image models can produce convincing pictures while failing to represent what a prompt actually requests. This paper separates that mismatch into two problems: concepts may be ignored entirely, or they may be assigned incorrectly within the image. The distinction matters because including a requested detail and attaching it to the right entity require different forms of correction.

CoMat is an end-to-end fine-tuning strategy that uses image-to-text concept matching to address both problems. Its concept activation module encourages the diffusion model to revisit concepts it has overlooked. A separate attribute concentration module connects each entity’s text conditions to the corresponding image region. Together, these modules target both missing content and incorrect placement of descriptive attributes.

Evaluations on three text-to-image alignment benchmarks show that CoMat-SDXL outperforms the SDXL baseline. The authors also report improved use of conditioning information and generalization to long, complex prompts without training specifically for those prompts. The findings suggest that strengthening concept matching can improve prompt adherence beyond the particular prompt complexity encountered during training.
neurips-2024-comat-aligning-text-to-imag.tldr: CoMat improves text-to-image alignment by teaching diffusion models to include overlooked concepts and assign attributes to the correct image regions.

paragraphs: Generating a molecule with a desired chemical property involves balancing two goals: moving toward that property and remaining within the distribution of meaningful molecular structures. Guidance that favors the target can interfere with the second goal. This paper addresses that tension in diffusion-based generation of three-dimensional molecules.

The authors introduce Time-Aware Conditional Synthesis, or TACS, which adds adaptively controlled guidance during generation. Its central component is the Time Correction Sampler. At each reverse diffusion step, this sampler controls the guidance while keeping the generated molecule on the appropriate manifold—the set of configurations consistent with that stage of the process. The approach therefore treats guidance strength and the evolving sample’s consistency as connected parts of generation.

The authors report strong performance in conditional 3D molecular generation, with validity and stability central to the method’s design. The broader significance is a promising route toward inverse molecular design: starting with desired properties and generating candidate structures. Potential benefits for drug discovery and materials science are presented as future possibilities, rather than demonstrated downstream outcomes.
neurips-2024-conditional-synthesis-of-3d.tldr: TACS uses adaptive guidance and a time-correcting diffusion sampler to target molecular properties while maintaining valid, stable 3D generation.

paragraphs: Constrained reinforcement learning asks an agent to earn reward while respecting additional requirements, such as safety constraints. Learning efficiently becomes difficult when the environment may contain infinitely many states. This paper studies a setting where every policy’s value functions can be represented linearly using a known feature map, an assumption called q-pi realizability.

Under a local-access model, the authors develop a primal-dual algorithm that jointly handles reward optimization and constraints. A specially designed off-policy evaluation procedure estimates policy values using historical data. Those estimates guide policy-gradient updates, allowing the algorithm to reuse information and conserve samples rather than treating each update as an entirely separate evaluation problem.

The algorithm produces, with high probability, a policy that strictly satisfies the constraints and nearly optimizes reward. Its iteration bound is polynomial in feature dimension and scales with the inverse cube of the target error, up to suppressed factors. The authors identify this as the first polynomial sample-complexity result for constrained MDPs under q-pi realizability. The guarantee depends on the stated representation and access assumptions.
neurips-2024-confident-natural-policy-gr.tldr: A primal-dual policy-gradient algorithm achieves polynomial sample complexity and high-probability constraint satisfaction under q-pi realizability and local access.

paragraphs: Audio-visual sound separation uses visual information to help distinguish sound sources. This paper introduces a continual version of the task: the model must learn new classes of sound sources while maintaining its ability to separate previously learned ones. That requirement reflects settings where unfamiliar sources keep appearing after initial training.

The challenge involves preserving connections between modalities as well as knowledge within each modality. A model may lose the relationship between what it sees and what it hears while adapting to new classes. The proposed ContAV-Sep method addresses this through a Cross-modal Similarity Distillation Constraint. It encourages the updated model to retain semantic similarity relationships between audio and visual information learned by earlier models.

The constraint can be incorporated into the training of different audio-visual separation frameworks. Experiments show that ContAV-Sep reduces catastrophic forgetting and significantly outperforms the compared continual learning baselines on this task. The results indicate that preserving cross-modal associations is a useful component of continual learning when successful predictions depend on matching sound with visual evidence.
neurips-2024-continual-audio-visual-soun.tldr: ContAV-Sep reduces forgetting during continual sound separation by preserving learned semantic relationships between audio and visual information.

paragraphs: This paper asks whether the stronger learning criterion of no swap regret yields stronger equilibrium convergence in repeated games. The distinction concerns actual behavior over rounds: a useful convergence result should explain how often players use strategies near equilibrium, beyond what aggregate performance alone reveals.

The authors prove that, in almost all symmetric zero-sum games with symmetric agent initialization, no-swap-regret self-play approaches a symmetric Nash equilibrium in a frequent-iterate sense. The fraction of rounds spent away from equilibrium vanishes. The conditions are consequential: allowing asymmetric initialization, an asymmetric game, or ordinary no-external-regret dynamics can invalidate the guarantee and permit non-equilibrating or chaotic behavior. This does not say that every such relaxation always produces chaos.

A second result identifies a requirement on the learner’s memory of rewards. General no-swap-regret learning cannot depend only on cumulative rewards, or on another order-insensitive summary of the observed reward set. It must use a time-asymmetric function of past rewards. Thus, the stronger regret criterion brings both a conditional convergence benefit and a structural requirement on how historical information influences decisions.
neurips-2024-convergence-of-no-swap-regr.tldr: No-swap-regret self-play has strong equilibrium convergence under specific symmetry conditions, while general no-swap-regret learning requires time-sensitive use of reward history.

paragraphs: An agent can learn reusable behaviors through unsupervised interaction, but those behaviors may be difficult to combine. When a single skill variable changes several parts of the environment at once, selecting it for one useful effect also brings other effects. This entanglement makes it harder to chain learned skills into solutions for later tasks.

Disentangled Unsupervised Skill Discovery, or DUSDi, divides skills into components intended to affect separate factors of the state space. Components can operate concurrently to produce low-level actions, while a hierarchical reinforcement learning system can chain them over time. The method uses a mutual-information objective to separate the influences of different components and value factorization to make optimization efficient.

Across the evaluated challenging environments, DUSDi learns disentangled skills and significantly outperforms prior skill discovery methods when transferring those skills to downstream tasks. The findings connect the organization of a skill library with its practical usefulness: skills become easier to reuse when their effects can be composed and sequenced without simultaneously controlling many unrelated state factors.
neurips-2024-disentangled-unsupervised-s.tldr: DUSDi learns separately controllable skill components that can be combined and chained more effectively for downstream reinforcement learning tasks.

paragraphs: Sparse fine-tuning adapts a pretrained model by changing selected weights that matter for a downstream task. Yet changing fewer weights does not automatically mean using little memory. The paper identifies two sources of overhead: storing the full weight matrix as learnable optimizer parameters and storing the indices that identify which weights can change.

SNELL addresses both costs. It represents the matrix used for sparse adaptation through two learnable low-rank matrices, reducing the need to store the full matrix as trainable parameters. A competition-based sparsification mechanism avoids storing tunable-weight indices. To preserve expressive capacity, nonlinear kernel functions are applied when combining the low-rank factors, increasing the rank of the resulting merged matrix.

Experiments across multiple downstream tasks report state-of-the-art performance with low memory usage. The contribution is therefore a combination of storage efficiency and adaptation capacity: a compact parameterization supports sparse changes without retaining the usual restriction of a purely low-rank merged update. The results support extending sparse parameter-efficient fine-tuning to larger pretrained vision models.
neurips-2024-expanding-sparse-tuning-for.tldr: SNELL combines compact low-rank parameters, nonlinear kernels, and competition-based sparsification to deliver strong sparse fine-tuning performance with low memory usage.

paragraphs: Implanted brain-computer interfaces decode intended behavior from neural recordings, potentially restoring movement and communication abilities. Neural signals can change over time, causing a previously effective decoder to fail. Recalibrating requires collecting new neural and behavioral data, creating a burden for users. Methods that need little or no explicit recalibration aim to reduce that burden.

FALCON provides a common benchmark for comparing these approaches. It brings together five datasets covering movement and communication behaviors relevant to intracortical interfaces. Each dataset includes initial calibration data, optional data for few-shot recalibration, and private evaluation data. This structure allows robustness to be assessed on unseen recordings while supporting approaches with different recalibration requirements.

The evaluation platform asks submitted code to return behavioral predictions, and the authors supply baseline methods from several approach families. The contribution is standardized evaluation infrastructure rather than a claim that decoder drift has been solved. By making comparisons more consistent, FALCON aims to provide stronger selection criteria for robust decoders and support their eventual translation into real-world devices.
neurips-2024-few-shot-algorithms-for-con.tldr: FALCON standardizes evaluation of neural decoders that aim to remain reliable as brain recordings change while requiring little or no recalibration.

paragraphs: Text-to-image systems can remain vulnerable to adversarial prompts despite moderation classifiers or fine-tuning intended to remove inappropriate concepts. This paper introduces GuardT2I, a moderation framework designed to improve robustness against prompts that induce inappropriate or not-safe-for-work imagery. Its focus is the information represented inside the generation system’s text guidance.

GuardT2I uses a large language model to conditionally translate text guidance embeddings into natural language. Rather than reducing its analysis immediately to a binary classification, it introduces a generative interpretation step for adversarial prompt detection. This makes the model’s internal guidance representation the basis for producing language that can support moderation.

The authors report that GuardT2I substantially outperforms OpenAI-Moderation and Microsoft Azure Moderator across the adversarial scenarios they evaluate, while preserving the underlying text-to-image model’s performance. These are experimental findings about the tested scenarios. The broader contribution is a moderation approach that uses generated language to expose information carried by guidance embeddings, offering another way to detect adversarial intent within a text-to-image pipeline.
neurips-2024-guardt2i-defending-text-to-.tldr: GuardT2I detects adversarial text-to-image prompts by translating internal guidance embeddings into natural language, with strong results across evaluated attacks.

paragraphs: Reinforcement learning in continuous state and action spaces needs structure to make learning manageable. Even when regret grows sublinearly with experience, a bound can be impractical if it depends exponentially on the planning horizon. This paper seeks a representation that supports both sublinear regret and polynomial dependence on that horizon.

The authors define Locally Linearizable MDPs, a class that generalizes linear MDPs and models with low inherent Bellman error. They introduce Cinderella, a no-regret algorithm for this representation class. Local linearity provides the organizing structure for the analysis, allowing the paper to connect several previously studied settings within one framework.

The authors show that all known learnable and feasible MDP families fit this class. Their argument passes through a family called Mildly Smooth MDPs, whose members admit suitable locally linearizable representations. Cinderella consequently obtains state-of-the-art regret bounds for previously known and some new continuous settings with these properties. The result unifies known positive cases; it does not establish that every possible learnable continuous environment must satisfy this representation.
neurips-2024-local-linearity-the-key-for.tldr: Cinderella achieves no-regret learning for locally linearizable MDPs, unifying known continuous settings with feasible dependence on the planning horizon.

paragraphs: Cooperative multi-agent learning becomes harder when agents need different behaviors. Updating agents sequentially gives each learner access to information from agents updated before it, creating an opportunity to guide exploration and specialization. This paper investigates how to use that preceding information explicitly, beyond merely assigning agents separate parameters.

Multi-Agent Divergence Policy Optimization, or MADPO, encourages two forms of policy difference. Intra-agent divergence measures changes between episodes to promote exploration. Inter-agent divergence measures differences between agents to encourage heterogeneous behavior. The method uses conditional Cauchy-Schwarz divergence to address stability and directionality concerns with traditional divergence measures and to supply exploration incentives guided by entropy.

Experiments on two challenging multi-agent tasks, each involving varied heterogeneous scenarios, show improvements over state-of-the-art sequential updating approaches. The findings suggest that sequential updates can be useful for more than organizing optimization: their information flow can actively shape exploration. MADPO connects that opportunity to explicit measures of behavioral change across time and behavioral diversity across cooperating agents.
neurips-2024-measuring-mutual-policy-div.tldr: MADPO improves sequential multi-agent exploration by encouraging policy diversity both across episodes and between agents.

paragraphs: Nanopore sequencing can produce long reads and directly measure modifications on DNA and RNA, but computational analysis accuracy remains a concern. The abstract highlights RNA base calling at approximately 90% accuracy against a stated aim of approximately 99.9%. It identifies a lack of integrated benchmark data as a barrier to broader machine learning contributions.

NanoBaseLib addresses that barrier by combining 16 public datasets containing more than 30 million reads for four analysis tasks. The authors process the raw data through a consistent workflow and store intermediate results in common formats. These choices give researchers a more uniform starting point for developing methods across the included datasets and tasks.

The project also evaluates baseline methods on test data and supplies a software package for accessing results. Its contribution is an integrated research resource, rather than a new method claimed to close the accuracy gap. Bringing data preparation, intermediate outputs, and reference evaluations together is intended to make entry into nanopore analysis easier and support more systematic method development.
neurips-2024-nanobaselib-a-multi-task-be.tldr: NanoBaseLib unifies more than 30 million nanopore reads, standardized processing, and baseline results to support machine learning research across four analysis tasks.

paragraphs: Controlling several objects in a generated scene requires specifying both their appearance and their individual positions and orientations. This paper introduces Neural Assets, per-object representations that replace text tokens as conditioning inputs to an image diffusion model. The goal is fine-grained control over each object’s three-dimensional pose and placement.

A Neural Asset pools visual information about an object from a reference image. During training, the model reconstructs that object in another image using its reference appearance together with its target pose. Separating the sources of appearance and pose information enables the model to learn distinct features for what an object looks like and where it belongs. The resulting representations retain the token-sequence interface used by existing text-to-image models.

After fine-tuning a pretrained diffusion model, the approach supports individual object editing and transfer or recomposition of assets across scenes. The authors report state-of-the-art multi-object editing on synthetic 3D scenes and the Objectron and Waymo Open video datasets. These results demonstrate the usefulness of object-level representations for controllable scene generation.
neurips-2024-neural-assets-3d-aware-mult.tldr: Neural Assets separate object appearance from target pose to enable precise multi-object editing and recomposition with image diffusion models.

paragraphs: 3D Gaussian Splatting can render realistic new views in real time, but its discrete, noisy primitives make accurate surface estimation difficult. Earlier attempts to regularize surface normals can reduce image quality because those normals are disconnected from the rendering process. Normal-GS addresses that disconnect by making normals directly participate in image formation.

The method models interactions between surface orientation and incoming light using a physically based rendering equation. It expresses surface colors through normals and an Integrated Directional Illumination Vector. An anchor-based representation implicitly shares these illumination vectors locally to improve memory use and simplify optimization. Optimized normals and Integrated Directional Encoding also help represent specular effects.

Experiments show near state-of-the-art visual quality together with accurate surface normals and retained real-time rendering. The central finding is that incorporating geometry into the rendering model can support both appearance and surface orientation estimates. The reported result is specifically strong normal estimation alongside rendering quality, rather than an unrestricted claim of perfect reconstruction or best performance on every measure.
neurips-2024-normal-gs-3d-gaussian-splat.tldr: Normal-GS integrates surface normals into Gaussian rendering to improve normal accuracy while retaining strong visual quality and real-time performance.

paragraphs: GFlowNets learn reusable samplers for distributions over objects assembled through a sequence of decisions. Although they are connected to hierarchical variational inference, traditional divergence-based training objectives have proved ineffective in earlier attempts. Common training methods instead minimize squared differences between log quantities associated with forward and backward policies. This paper investigates the gap between the theoretical connection and practical training.

The authors first extend the connection beyond discrete distributions to arbitrary measurable topological spaces. They then provide empirical evidence that high variance in stochastic gradient estimates explains the difficulty of divergence-based learning. To reduce that noise, they develop control variates based on the REINFORCE leave-one-out estimator and prove that these adjustments reduce variance.

Experiments suggest that the resulting algorithms often converge faster than previous approaches. That is a qualified empirical finding, rather than a guarantee of faster training in every setting. The broader contribution is to make divergence minimization a more practical route for GFlowNet training, bringing its algorithms closer to the variational inference framework already linked to them theoretically.
neurips-2024-on-divergence-measures-for-.tldr: Variance-reducing gradient estimators make divergence-based GFlowNet training more effective and often accelerate convergence in the reported experiments.

paragraphs: Bayesian persuasion studies how an informed sender can influence a receiver by choosing what payoff-relevant information to reveal. In the online version, the interaction repeats and the sender can learn over time. This paper removes prior knowledge assumptions used in earlier work: the sender initially knows neither the distribution over states of nature nor the receiver’s utilities.

The proposed algorithm searches a suitable space of signaling schemes to learn the receiver’s best responses. Its key device is a nonstandard representation of those schemes that allows learning despite the missing prior and utility information. The representation makes it possible to organize the search without first assuming the information the sender is trying to discover.

The authors prove sublinear regret relative to an optimal signaling scheme, so the average performance gap decreases as the number of rounds grows. Matching lower bounds establish that the algorithm’s guarantees are tight. The results also yield upper and lower sample-complexity bounds for a related PAC-learning problem, connecting repeated persuasion with learning a signaling scheme from limited observations.
neurips-2024-online-bayesian-persuasion-.tldr: An online persuasion algorithm achieves tight sublinear-regret guarantees without prior knowledge of the state distribution or receiver utilities.

paragraphs: Semi-supervised continual learning must preserve old knowledge while learning from both labeled and unlabeled data. Distillation can help, but preserving individual representations or pairwise similarities becomes difficult when unlabeled information is noisy and the feature space changes substantially. This paper proposes preserving structural information that is more stable under such noise.

Persistence Homology Distillation, or PsHD, captures how structural features evolve across different scales in visual data. Its multiscale construction provides stability against noise interference. The authors turn these features into a distillation loss and introduce an acceleration algorithm to reduce the cost of computing persistence homology. This makes the structural preservation objective more practical within continual training.

The paper supplies theoretical and experimental evidence of greater stability than representation-based and pairwise-similarity distillation. Across three datasets, it reports an average improvement of 3.9% over the state of the art. It also reports a 1.5% improvement while reducing memory-buffer size by 60%. These findings support the potential of multiscale structural information for retaining knowledge and making better use of unlabeled data.
neurips-2024-persistence-homology-distil.tldr: PsHD preserves noise-stable, multiscale structural information to improve semi-supervised continual learning, including results with a substantially smaller memory buffer.

paragraphs: Scaling studies compare how model performance changes with training resources, so the ability to evaluate different training durations matters. This paper argues that reliance on cosine learning-rate schedules makes those studies unnecessarily expensive. Because the schedule is tied to a chosen duration, exploring several durations at the same model size requires less reusable training.

The authors investigate a constant learning rate followed by cooldown periods as a direct alternative. They find that this approach scales predictably and reliably, similarly to cosine scheduling. They also study stochastic weight averaging, which combines model weights from training, and report improved performance along the training trajectory across scales without additional training costs.

Together, these findings allow scaling experiments to use fewer, reusable training runs and substantially reduce compute and GPU hours. The contribution concerns the design of the experimental process as much as model optimization. A schedule that supports reuse can make it cheaper to study how performance depends on training duration and to inform decisions about future training setups and architectures.
neurips-2024-scaling-laws-and-compute-op.tldr: Constant learning rates with cooldowns enable reusable scaling runs, while weight averaging improves performance without additional training costs.

paragraphs: Predicting properties of a neural network from its parameters requires an encoder that can handle the network’s structure. Existing approaches can require separate encoders for different architectures. This paper introduces the Set-based Neural Network Encoder, or SNE, to represent networks with mixed architectures and different parameter counts within one approach.

SNE uses set-to-set and set-to-vector functions while accounting for the hierarchy of neural computation. It uses Logit Invariance to learn the minimal invariance properties required by symmetries in weight space. A pad-chunk-encode pipeline processes layers in a way that can be adjusted to available computation and memory, connecting the representation method with practical resource constraints.

The authors also introduce two transfer tasks. Cross-dataset prediction tests transfer between model collections trained on different datasets with the same architecture. Cross-architecture prediction tests transfer to architectures absent during training. SNE outperforms relevant baselines on standard benchmarks. The work therefore combines a more flexible weight encoder with evaluation settings that ask whether property prediction transfers beyond the model collection used to train it.
neurips-2024-set-based-neural-network-en.tldr: SNE uses set-based representations to encode networks of varying architectures and sizes for property prediction, outperforming relevant benchmark baselines.

paragraphs: Conditional neural fields can represent solutions to partial differential equations continuously in space and time without depending on a fixed grid. However, evolving those solutions through an unconstrained latent representation can make it difficult to enforce known physical structure. This paper focuses on retaining the geometric information needed to preserve the equation’s symmetries.

The proposed framework models solution evolution as flows of point clouds over the relevant symmetry group. Preserving geometry in the conditional neural field’s latent space allows the forecast to respect known symmetries of the PDE. The method combines continuous querying with a structured internal representation, rather than relying only on the flexibility of a latent dynamics model.

The authors report improved generalization and data efficiency. Their evaluations show generalization to previously unseen spatial and temporal locations and to geometric transformations of initial conditions, including cases where other neural-field forecasting approaches fail. Results also improve over baselines on several challenging geometries. These findings support symmetry-preserving latent dynamics as a useful way to make continuous PDE forecasts transfer across coordinates and transformed inputs.
neurips-2024-space-time-continuous-pde-f.tldr: Geometry-preserving latent dynamics help continuous neural-field PDE forecasts respect symmetries and generalize to unseen locations and transformed initial conditions.

paragraphs: Explaining a black-box predictor through human-understandable concepts can make its behavior easier to discuss. Yet an importance score alone does not establish whether a reported relationship is statistically credible. This paper addresses the need for rigorous testing when identifying semantic concepts associated with a model’s predictions.

The authors define concept importance through conditional independence at two levels: globally across a population and locally for an individual sample. This formulation turns importance into a statistical question that can be tested. They use sequential kernelized independence testing to derive a ranking of concepts, connecting interpretability with an explicit framework for evaluating evidence.

The framework is demonstrated on synthetic datasets and image classification with several vision-language models. These experiments illustrate its effectiveness and flexibility across the considered settings. The contribution is a way to give semantic explanations a statistical foundation, motivated by the need to control false positives and false discoveries. Its importance statements concern conditional statistical relationships with predictions; the abstract does not present them as causal explanations of the model or the world.
neurips-2024-testing-semantic-importance.tldr: The paper formalizes semantic concept importance using conditional independence and applies sequential testing to rank concepts relevant to black-box predictions.

paragraphs: Sparse ridge regression combines a restriction on how many coefficients are used with ridge regularization. OKRidge is an existing algorithm described as faster and more accurate than earlier approaches, but its estimation error lacked a theoretical analysis. This paper focuses on providing that analysis so the method’s accuracy has a stronger mathematical foundation.

The authors express OKRidge’s estimation error as a Primary Optimization problem. They then use the Convex Gaussian min-max theorem to obtain a simpler Auxiliary Optimization problem. Analyzing this auxiliary problem gives a route to characterizing the original estimator’s error. The main contribution is therefore an analytical reformulation and the error theory derived from it, rather than a replacement algorithm.

Experiments are used to check the resulting theorems, and the authors report close agreement between observed behavior and theoretical findings. That agreement supports the analysis as an account of OKRidge’s estimation error in the studied setting. It strengthens the theoretical basis for using an already effective method by connecting its computational procedure to predictions about estimation accuracy.
neurips-2024-the-reliability-of-okridge-.tldr: The paper develops an estimation-error analysis for OKRidge using the Convex Gaussian min-max theorem and finds close experimental agreement with its theory.

paragraphs: Controlling motion in generated video often requires additional training, and methods may need retraining for different model architectures. This paper asks what motion information is already present inside video diffusion models. Understanding those internal features could provide a basis for both interpreting motion and controlling it without a new training stage.

Using principal component analysis, the authors identify robust motion-aware information in existing model features. They construct MOFT, a motion feature representation that removes content-correlated information and filters motion channels. The resulting representation is designed to expose motion more clearly, can be extracted without training, and generalizes across diverse architectures.

The authors then use MOFT in a training-free framework for video motion control. They report competitive performance in generating natural motion that follows the intended control. The work links an analysis of internal representations to a practical generation method: separating motion information from content provides an interpretable control signal already available in the model. Its reported performance is competitive, rather than a claim of universal superiority over trained alternatives.
neurips-2024-video-diffusion-models-are-.tldr: MOFT extracts interpretable motion features already present in video diffusion models and uses them for competitive motion control without additional training.

paragraphs: Language and vision-language agents benefit from strong examples in their prompts, but useful demonstrations can be difficult to construct. In-Context Abstraction Learning, or ICAL, builds such examples from imperfect demonstrations and human feedback. It turns experience into a growing memory that agents can retrieve for later decisions.

A vision-language model converts a demonstrated trajectory into a generalized program, correcting inefficient actions and annotating causal relationships, object changes, temporal subgoals, and relevant visual details. The agent attempts the trajectory in a similar environment, and human feedback iteratively improves the abstraction. These richer examples help the agent use the structure of an experience, beyond simply copying its action sequence.

ICAL improves performance on TEACh, VisualWebArena, and Ego4D. Reported results include a 12.6% improvement in TEACh goal-condition success and VisualWebArena task success rising from 14.3% to 22.7% with GPT4V. On Ego4D, it improves over few-shot GPT-4V and remains competitive with supervised models. As memory grows, the agent needs less feedback and fewer interactions per demonstration; fine-tuning brings additional gains.
neurips-2024-vlm-agents-generate-their-o.tldr: ICAL turns imperfect demonstrations and human feedback into reusable, abstracted memories that improve agent decisions and reduce subsequent feedback needs.
